issue.title: Filter the device list by site and role
issue.body: The NOC dashboard lists thousands of devices. GET /devices should accept optional query parameters site and role (for example ?site=sjc&role=router) and return only matching devices, still sorted by ID. With no parameters it behaves as today.

requirements.summary: Add optional site and role query-parameter filters to GET /devices so the NOC dashboard can narrow the device list, keeping the no-parameter behavior and ID ordering unchanged.
requirements: GET /devices accepts optional query parameters site and role.
When site is provided, only devices whose site equals that value are returned.
When role is provided, only devices whose role equals that value are returned.
When both are provided, only devices matching both are returned.
With no parameters, the endpoint returns the same results as the current implementation.
All returned devices are sorted by ID in ascending order, filtered or not.
Filtering does not change the HTTP status code for valid requests, which remains 200.
acceptance_criteria: GET /devices with no query parameters returns the same set and ordering of devices as the current behavior, sorted by ID, with HTTP 200.
GET /devices?site=sjc returns HTTP 200 and only devices whose site equals sjc; a Go test seeding devices at sjc and another site asserts no other-site device appears.
GET /devices?role=router returns HTTP 200 and only devices whose role equals router.
GET /devices?site=sjc&role=router returns HTTP 200 and only devices matching both site sjc and role router; a Go test asserts a device matching only one of the two is excluded.
Results from any filtered request remain sorted in ascending ID order; a Go test with out-of-order seeded IDs asserts the returned IDs are ascending.
GET /devices?site=nosuch returns HTTP 200 with an empty device list when no device matches; a Go test asserts an empty result rather than an error.
Filter values are matched exactly and case-sensitively; a Go test asserts ?site=SJC does not match devices with site sjc.
An empty parameter value such as ?site= is treated as absent, so it returns the same result as no site filter; a Go test asserts this.
assumptions: Site and role are exact string matches against the device's stored site and role fields, with no wildcard or prefix matching.
Matching is case-sensitive because the issue gives no normalization rule.
An empty query value is treated the same as an omitted parameter.
Unknown site or role values return an empty list with HTTP 200 rather than a 400 error, since the issue does not define validation.
The response shape and pagination behavior stay as they are today; the issue does not ask for pagination changes.
Each device record has site and role fields that the filter can read.
out_of_scope: Adding pagination, limit, or offset parameters to GET /devices.
Filtering by any parameter other than site and role, such as status or vendor.
Multi-value filters such as ?site=sjc,sfo or repeated parameters.
Case-insensitive or fuzzy matching of site and role values.
Changes to the dashboard UI or any client code that calls the endpoint.
Changes to how devices are stored, created, or updated.

plan.reason: Small, self-contained change to the store and handler. It needs no new dependencies and does not touch auth, CI or go.mod. The requirements are consistent.
steps: In store.go, add func (s *Store) ListFiltered(site, role string) []Device. An empty value means no filter for that field. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Take the read lock and return results sorted by ID, reusing the same sort as List.
Leave List unchanged, or have it delegate to ListFiltered("", "") without changing its signature or behaviour.
In http.go, the GET /devices handler reads r.URL.Query().Get("site") and Get("role"), calls s.ListFiltered, and writes 200 with the existing response shape. Keep the handler thin.
Make sure an empty filtered result encodes as an empty JSON array [], not null. Return a non-nil slice from ListFiltered.
Add table-driven tests in inventory_test.go for the store and for HTTP via httptest.
Run gofmt, go vet and go test.
test_plan: TestStoreListFiltered (table-driven): seed devices with out-of-order IDs across sites sjc/sfo and roles router/switch. Cases: no filters (equals List), site=sjc, role=router, site=sjc+role=router (excludes a device matching only one), site=nosuch (empty), site=SJC (no match, case-sensitive). Assert IDs are ascending in every case.

TestHTTPListFilter (table-driven, httptest): GET /devices with no params, ?site=sjc, ?role=router, ?site=sjc&role=router, ?site=nosuch, ?site=SJC and ?site=. Assert status 200 and the exact ordered ID list for each.
Assert ?site=nosuch returns a JSON empty array, not null or an error.
Assert ?site= returns the same result as no params.
Existing tests TestHTTPFlow and TestStoreListDelete still pass unchanged.
